successCriteria.description: `npm run build` (tsc --noEmit) exits 0 with the two new files present, under strict TypeScript (no implicit any, strict null checks).

`ReadinessState` exists in src/modules/uptime/uptime.model.ts with exactly two members whose values are the lowercase hyphenated wire literals `READY = 'ready'` and `NOT_READY = 'not-ready'`; no third member (DEGRADED/UNKNOWN/PENDING) is present.
`ReadinessStatus` is declared with `status: ReadinessState` as its sole field — no timestamp, no error, no diagnostic field — and is not exported from src/shared/types/.

`ReadinessProbe` is declared with exactly `id: string`, `startedAt: Date`, `completedAt: Date | null`, `outcome: ReadinessState | null`, `failureReason: unknown | null`, and is never serialized into an HTTP body.
`IReadinessRepository` exists in src/modules/uptime/uptime.repository.interface.ts with exactly one method `check(): Promise<void>` — no optional trailing PoolClient parameter, no other method.

`PgReadinessRepository` in src/modules/uptime/uptime.repository.ts implements `IReadinessRepository` and is the only file in the phase that contains the connectivity query; it consumes the shared pool from src/shared/db and opens no second pool.

The readiness query timeout is a module-level named constant (e.g. READINESS_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000) referenced by the query; no numeric timeout literal appears inline at the call site and the pool's connectionTimeoutMillis is not relied upon.
`IUptimeService` declares `checkReadiness(): Promise<ReadinessStatus>` alongside the unchanged `getUptime(): UptimeStatus`, and `UptimeService` implements both.

`UptimeService` accepts a constructor-injected `IReadinessRepository` that defaults to a `PgReadinessRepository` instance, so `new UptimeService()` still compiles and the service never imports the pool, a client, or a module-level db helper.

`checkReadiness()` resolves to `{ status: ReadinessState.READY }` when the probe resolves and to `{ status: ReadinessState.NOT_READY }` when the probe rejects; it never throws and the rejection value never appears in the returned object.
Two consecutive `checkReadiness()` calls each invoke the probe (call count equals call count of checkReadiness) — no cached or memoized result is returned.

src/modules/uptime/index.ts re-exports ReadinessStatus, ReadinessState, ReadinessProbe, IReadinessRepository and PgReadinessRepository in addition to the pre-existing UptimeStatus, IUptimeService, UptimeService and uptimeRoutes exports.

The existing /uptime behaviour is unchanged: `getUptime()` still returns `{ uptimeSeconds: Math.floor(process.uptime()) }`, uptime.routes.ts is not modified in this phase, and no route is registered for readiness.
No test file is added or modified in this phase (tests/unit/modules/uptime/ does not gain a file), and `npx jest --passWithNoTests` still exits 0.

constraints: Extend the existing src/modules/uptime/ module in place. Do NOT create a new module, do NOT create a shared health/readiness abstraction, and do NOT touch src/modules/status/ (pre-existing, unreconciled, out of scope).

Consume the single existing pg Pool via the public entry point src/shared/db/index.ts (or src/shared/db/connection.ts, as PgLeaveRequestRepository does). Never open a second pool, never add a dependency, never introduce an ORM.

The connectivity query is written in exactly one place — PgReadinessRepository. It must not be added as a `ping()` on any domain repository, must not be promoted to src/shared/db/, and must not read or write any domain table.

The readiness query carries its own explicit 2000ms timeout, declared as a module-level NAMED constant, never inline and never delegated to the pool's connectionTimeoutMillis or a caller's deadline. On timeout the rejection is indistinguishable from a rejected query.

A successful ROUND TRIP is required: acquiring a client is not sufficient, the query must return. No retry, no error swallowing, no logging inside the repository (the route owns request.log.error in Phase 2).
NO caching and NO memoization anywhere in the probe or the service — every call performs the check. The probe is stateless and per-request; it holds no state between calls.
`checkReadiness()` must not throw and must not place the raw error (or any diagnostic detail) in the returned value. The rejection is caught and mapped to NOT_READY.

Readiness is a pure observation, not a state-changing operation: no audit record (GP-002 does not apply), no entity mutation, no transaction, and IUnitOfWork is not involved. The probe must never join a caller's transaction.
ReadinessStatus / ReadinessState / ReadinessProbe are module-local to src/modules/uptime/ — do NOT promote them to src/shared/types/ (single-module use).
Keep the existing UptimeStatus interface and getUptime() unchanged; the existing `new UptimeService()` call site in uptime.routes.ts must keep compiling without editing that file.
Strict TypeScript: no implicit any, strict null checks; use `unknown` with type guards rather than `any` (HARNESS.json constraint `no-any`). No hardcoded secrets.

Module boundaries: modules import only from another module's index.ts; dependencies flow inward (routes → service → repository interface → shared-db). The uptime module must not import from src/shared/errors/ (the /ready body carries no error shape).
outOfScope: The GET /ready HTTP route and its 200/503 mapping — deferred to Phase 2. uptime.routes.ts must not be modified in this phase.
Adding '/ready' to PUBLIC_PATHS in src/shared/auth/index.ts — deferred to Phase 2 (must land with the route or the probe 401s).
Unit tests for checkReadiness (tests/unit/modules/uptime/uptime.service.test.ts) — deferred to Phase 3; no test file is added or modified here.
src/modules/status/ (SystemStatus, StatusService.getStatus()) — pre-existing, unreconciled dead code; not used, extended, or reconciled.
Any persistence: no migration, no readiness_checks / probe-history / audit table, no change to any existing table. sqlSchemas is intentionally empty.
Any change to /uptime semantics, to the shared pool configuration, to IUnitOfWork, or to the shared error types.
Caching/TTL of the readiness result, retries, degraded/partial readiness, and any check beyond the single connectivity query (disk, memory, downstream services, migrations, schema version).

ambiguities.description: The reconciled architecture lists ReadinessProbe lifecycle states PENDING / SUCCEEDED / FAILED, but the phase spec fixes ReadinessState to exactly two members and the probe's `outcome` field is typed `ReadinessState | null`. The probe states are therefore not enum members.
options: Derive PENDING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED from field nullness (completedAt/outcome null = PENDING) with no extra enum members — the phase spec's two-member constraint wins
Add PENDING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED as a separate probe-state enum distinct from ReadinessState
Treat the architecture's probe-state list as descriptive prose only and model no probe state at all

ambiguities.description: The phase spec requires a 2000ms query timeout owned by the readiness check, but does not say whether the timeout must be enforced by the driver (pg query_timeout / statement_timeout) or by a race in the repository. The observable requirement is only that a hung query rejects like any other failure.
options: Enforce via the pg query config (query_timeout) on the single query
Enforce via a Promise.race against a timer in the repository
Either is acceptable provided the rejection is indistinguishable from a query failure and the constant is module-level and named

ambiguities.description: The phase spec says the repository consumes the shared pool "imported from src/shared/db", while the reconciled architecture says the concrete repository takes a constructor-injected `dbPool: Pool = defaultPool` "exactly as PgLeaveRequestRepository does". Both are satisfiable, but the spec's wording could be read as a direct module-level import with no injection seam.
options: Constructor-injected `dbPool: Pool = defaultPool` imported from the shared db entry point (matches PgLeaveRequestRepository and the reconciled architecture)
Direct module-level import of the shared pool with no constructor parameter
Either, provided no second pool is created and the shared pool is the only source

ambiguities.description: The phase spec says ReadinessProbe is added to uptime.model.ts with the canonical field shape, but does not say whether the probe is actually instantiated/populated by the service or repository in this phase, or whether the type is declared now and wired in a later phase. The architecture describes it as transient and per-request.
options: Declare the type only; the service maps probe resolution/rejection directly to ReadinessStatus without materialising a ReadinessProbe
Materialise a ReadinessProbe per checkReadiness() call (id, startedAt, completedAt, outcome, failureReason) even though it is never serialized
Leave the decision to the code agent as long as the type exists with the exact shape and never reaches the HTTP body

entityInvariants.invariant: Exactly two members, both terminal, both lowercase hyphenated string literals whose value IS the wire value: READY = 'ready' and NOT_READY = 'not-ready'. No third member (DEGRADED, UNKNOWN, PENDING) may be added — the enum is the response contract. The probe is binary and total: any rejection (connection refused, auth failure, timeout, pool exhaustion) maps to NOT_READY without discrimination.

A value object with `status: ReadinessState` as its sole field — no identity, no timestamp, no diagnostic detail, no error information. It is the complete and only payload of the readiness response and is never persisted or enriched. Module-local to src/modules/uptime/uptime.model.ts.

Transient and per-request: created, settles, discarded within the evaluation. Never persisted, never cached, never shared between requests. Its lifecycle states PENDING → SUCCEEDED / PENDING → FAILED are derived from field nullness (completedAt/outcome null while PENDING), NOT from additional ReadinessState members; both terminal states are final and a probe is never re-entered, retried, or reused. failureReason is domain-internal and never crosses the HTTP boundary.

Stateless and holds no result between calls: every check() performs a fresh round trip against the shared pool. It owns no entity and persists nothing; it is the only place the connectivity query is written.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: None — internal data-access interface, not reachable from the HTTP boundary.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Resolves (void) only when the connectivity query round trip succeeds; rejects with the underlying pg error otherwise, including on the 2000ms timeout. No retry, no error swallowing, no logging, no wrapping into a domain error type. Takes no optional trailing PoolClient — the probe must always acquire from the shared pool so it can never join a caller's transaction.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: None at this layer — the endpoint's unauthenticated status is a Phase 2 concern (PUBLIC_PATHS).
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Never rejects and never throws: probe resolution maps to { status: ReadinessState.READY }, any probe rejection maps to { status: ReadinessState.NOT_READY }. The raw error is never placed in the returned value. Every call performs the check — no caching, no memoization.
Unchanged: returns { uptimeSeconds: Math.floor(process.uptime()) } and never touches the database. Must remain byte-for-byte compatible with the existing /uptime behaviour.

Accepts an IReadinessRepository defaulting to a PgReadinessRepository instance so the existing zero-argument construction site keeps compiling; the service must never import the pool, a client, or a module-level db helper.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Consume the shared pool exactly as the existing repositories do — import the pool from the shared db entry point and accept it as a constructor-injected `dbPool: Pool = defaultPool`; never construct a new Pool.
The shared pool is the single pg Pool exported from the shared db entry point; the readiness repository must consume it through that public entry point rather than reaching into connection internals.

The module's file layout must follow the existing split-file convention already used by this module (model / repository.interface / repository / service.interface / service / index), not the single-file `<name>.{model,repository,service}.ts` shape.

The public entry point must keep re-exporting the pre-existing symbols (UptimeStatus, IUptimeService, UptimeService, uptimeRoutes) and add the new ones in the same `export { X } from './file'` style — no default exports, no barrel re-export of internals.
The service must keep the existing class shape (class implementing its interface, methods returning the model types) and the existing `getUptime()` body must remain unchanged.

The interface must keep the existing `getUptime(): UptimeStatus` declaration unchanged and add `checkReadiness(): Promise<ReadinessStatus>` to the same interface — no second service interface, no renamed method.
The existing UptimeStatus interface must remain unchanged in the same file that gains the readiness types; the new types are added alongside it, not in a new model file.

The reconciled architecture is the source of truth for this feature's entity shapes, module boundaries, repository naming (IReadinessRepository / PgReadinessRepository with check(): Promise<void>) and the deliberate divergence that check() takes no optional PoolClient. Any deviation must be flagged, not silently taken.

The feature's binding business rules (binary/total probe, no caching, no transaction, no audit, fixed body, module-local types) are recorded in the architecture document's readiness section and must be honoured; the section must be updated to record this phase's delivery.
The readiness probe is a pure observation: it must not be routed through IUnitOfWork and must not import it — the unit of work exists for service-owned write transactions only.
The readiness types must NOT be promoted to the shared types module — that module owns cross-module enums and DTOs only, and ReadinessStatus is consumed by exactly one module.

integrationPoints.why: The readiness repository's only data-access dependency; the shared pool must be consumed through this public entry point, never re-created.
The existing `new UptimeService()` call site must keep compiling unchanged; Phase 2 will add the readiness handler here.
The module's public surface that Phase 2 (route) and Phase 3 (tests) consume; the new symbols must be reachable from it.
Phase 2 adds '/ready' to the default-deny public-path set; this phase must not touch it but must not make that addition impossible.
The constructor-injected IReadinessRepository is the seam the Phase 3 unit tests substitute with a fake; the injection must be usable without touching the pool.
